content:
Apple has revealed further details about the Apple Music AI labelling requirements it first announced back in March.

AI-generated content will be clearly marked on Apple Music.

Earlier this year, Apple announced Apple Music would require AI transparency disclosures on new cover art, songs, compositions, and music videos submitted to the service.

Now Apple has shared more details about how this system will work.

In an email to creators today, Apple said: "Later this year, we will also surface these disclosures to Apple Music listeners as a 'Made With AI' label."

Apple has also clarified which situations require these disclosures. The email reads:

Apple Music adds that the goal of this measure is "to provide as much transparency as possible to listeners," and points creators to its Music Style Guide for details.

Apple Music's approach is just the latest example of streaming platforms responding to the proliferation of AI-generated music—as more musicians incorporate generative AI into their production workflows, platforms have been forced to grapple with the issue.

Spotify has previously said it will, by default, exclude AI-impersonated music from editorial recommendations and algorithmic suggestions; Deezer also announced last year that songs generated entirely by AI will not appear in its recommendations or editorial playlists. Deezer even claimed last month that fully AI-generated music accounted for over half of the platform's daily new uploads for the first time.

On the Apple Music side, platform head Oliver Schusser previously revealed on Billboard's On the Record podcast that while more than a third of the music uploaded to Apple Music each month is fully AI-generated, it accounts for under 0.5% of listens on the platform.
